candidates.title: Manual's PMA flag layout (E bit; R/W/X/IR/IW/DID bit positions) does not match the PMA entries the emulator writes into the guest-readable PMA array and decodes
candidates.component: State layout / interpreter and state-access layers (PMA entries) versus the manual (doc/README.md, 'PMAs')
candidates.role: Honest operator (interpreter, state-access layers: the transition function and its state layout, R13); the manual is the specification the threat model refers to
candidates.location: doc/README.md 'PMAs' section, lines 7906-7921 (first-word table at 7913-7915: bits 63-12 start, 11-8 DID, 7 IW, 6 IR, 5 X, 4 W, 3 R, 2 E, 1 IO, 0 M; 'The M, IO, and E bits are mutually exclusive'); src/pmas-constants.hpp lines 34-55 (PMA_ISTART_M_SHIFT=0, IO=1, R=2, W=3, X=4, IR=5, IW=6, DID=7 with a 5-bit mask, no E bit anywhere in src/); src/machine-address-ranges.cpp (pmas_flags of every range); src/find-pma.hpp / address ranges decoded by the interpreter (native and uarch).
candidates.description: The manual specifies the first word of each PMA record as M(0) IO(1) E(2) R(3) W(4) X(5) IR(6) IW(7) DID(11-8). The emulator encodes and decodes it as M(0) IO(1) R(2) W(3) X(4) IR(5) IW(6) DID(11-7): there is no E (excluded) bit, every permission bit sits one position lower and DID is 5 bits wide starting at bit 7. The PMA array at 0x10000 is hashed state, is guest-readable (its own PMA is R), and the manual presents it as the way the available ranges and their attributes are discovered at runtime ('These words are readable both internally and externally'). Decoded as the manual says, every range of every machine is 'excluded' with M and E both set (which the manual says cannot happen), a writable flash drive and the tx buffer are 'not writable, executable', and the rx buffer, a read-only flash drive and the PMA array itself are 'not readable, executable'. The driver ids also come out wrong (RAM -> 0 'empty', flash -> 1 'memory', rx buffer -> 3 'flash drive'). The interpreter enforces the code layout, so the permissions the guest actually gets differ from the ones the PMA entries declare under the manual's layout.
candidates.trigger: No adversary action is needed: any guest (kernel, hypervisor-less OS, bare-metal runtime) or any independent implementation or reviewer of the transition function that reads the PMA array following the manual gets wrong memory permissions and driver ids. An input sender benefits once a guest sets up its own protection (page-table permissions, W^X, which ranges untrusted code may map) from the manual-decoded flags.
candidates.reachability: Every machine: the PMA entries are written at creation from fixed flags and are read-only to the guest, so the mismatch holds at every reachable state of every valid template.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no. It needs no excluded trigger (no API misuse, no foreign snapshot, no deployment violation); the manual is 'the specification [the threat model] refers to'.

2. Role: the state layout and the interpreter's PMA decoding are the transition function (AUDIT.md table: 'Interpreter, state-access layers, ... Honest operator'); R13 lists 'The state layout' as part of the protocol.

3. High/Medium cases: fits "An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)." if no correct guest reads the PMA flag words; and section 8 adds "A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right."

4. Critical: if the manual were right, R8 fails at every reachable state: "The main processor reaches only the ranges that the PMA entries declare, with the declared permissions." (flash drive and tx buffer declared non-writable but writable; rx buffer and read-only flash declared unreadable but readable; all ranges declared excluded), and R7 lists "Address translation and memory permissions" among the areas where "any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths."

5. Low: not applicable (a rule is violated under either reading). Two readings: Medium (documentation is stale, no shipped guest decodes PMA flags) versus Critical (the manual defines the layout; the behaviour is rated as if it were right). Deciding fact: whether a correct guest or an independent implementation is entitled to decode the guest-readable PMA array as the manual documents it.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Critical under the 'as if the manual were right' reading of section 8 with R8/R7)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not change any hash or proof. It violates R7/R8 as the manual defines them: a correct guest that derives memory permissions from the PMA array (the manual's stated purpose for it) grants or denies the wrong access, e.g. treats the tx buffer and flash drives as read-only+executable and the rx buffer as unreadable+executable, which is exactly the isolation/data-integrity reliance R7 protects; an independent implementation of the state layout built from the manual (R13) would decode PMAs differently from the deployed uarch.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERSPEC/pma.lua and pma-access.lua against the in-tree build. PMA words: RAM 0x80000000 flags=0x0fd, flash rw 0x1ed, flash ro 0x1a5, tx 0x46d, rx 0x3e5, PMA array 0x0a5, HTIF 0x28e. Manual decode of 0x1ed: E=1 R=1 W=0 X=1 DID=1; of 0x3e5: E=1 R=0 W=0 X=1 DID=3. One-instruction probes in M-mode (ld/sd/fetch at the range start): flash rw is actually R=1 W=1 X=0, rx is R=1 W=0 X=0, read-only flash R=1 W=0 X=0, PMA array R=1 W=0 X=0. All 7 memory entries differ from the manual decode ('entries whose manual-decoded permissions differ from the behavior: 7'). grep finds no E/excluded bit in src/.
candidates.test_idea: Lua: create a machine with RAM, one writable and one read-only flash drive; read each PMA record with read_memory(AR_PMAS_START + 16*i); decode the first word with the manual's table; assert (a) no record has E set together with M or IO, (b) the decoded DID equals the documented driver id of the range (RAM 1, flash 3, rx 7, tx 8), and (c) the decoded R/W/X equal what a one-instruction ld/sd/fetch probe of the range does. Fails on audit/prt2; passes once the manual's table or the encoding is corrected.

candidates.title: Undocumented Zcb: the emulator executes compressed encodings that are reserved in the documented RV64IMAFDC ISA, including c.sext.b/c.zext.h/c.sext.h/c.zext.w that Zcb itself only defines when Zbb/Zba exist
candidates.component: Interpreter (instruction decoding), src/interpret.cpp and the generated jump table
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp execute_C_LBU..execute_C_MUL (lines ~5266-5389) and INSN_CASE(C_LBU)..INSN_CASE(C_MUL) (6126-6162); tools/gen-interpret-jump-table.lua 'Zcb quadrant 0' (line 248) and 'Zcb quadrant 1' (line 358); doc/README.md line 7306-7312 ('implements the RV64IMAFDCZicsr_Zifencei ISA'); src/dtb.cpp misa_to_isa_string (riscv,isa = rv64acdfimsu, no zcb).
candidates.description: The manual states the main processor implements RV64IMAFDC_Zicsr_Zifencei and documents no other extension; misa and the device tree advertise no more. The interpreter nevertheless decodes the Zcb encodings (c.lbu, c.lhu, c.lh, c.sb, c.sh, c.zext.b, c.sext.b, c.zext.h, c.sext.h, c.zext.w, c.not, c.mul). In the documented ISA all of them are reserved and must raise an illegal-instruction exception. Moreover the ratified Zc specification makes c.sext.b, c.zext.h and c.sext.h available only when Zbb is implemented and c.zext.w only when Zba is implemented; the emulator implements neither (the 32-bit sext.b and add.uw trap as illegal), yet executes the four compressed forms. The manual documents no deviation (CHANGELOG.md mentions Zcb, the manual does not).
candidates.trigger: Any guest code, at any privilege level, that executes one of these 16-bit encodings: it runs instead of trapping. An input sender reaches it through any guest that relies on the illegal-instruction trap for reserved encodings (trap-and-emulate, instruction filtering of untrusted code, or a test of the documented ISA).
candidates.reachability: Any state whose pc points at such an encoding; guest memory is guest-writable, so always reachable.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no (emulator behaviour triggered by guest instructions).
2. Role: interpreter = Honest operator; consistent between native and uarch (same source).

3. High/Medium cases: matches "An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)." The instructions are unprivileged, act only on the executing context's registers and pass the normal memory checks, so I found no isolation break.

4. Critical: only under a strict reading of R7: "The emulator implements the RISC-V specification and the devices as the manual documents them, departing only where the manual documents a deviation." together with the listed area 'Traps and interrupts' (a mandated illegal-instruction trap is not raised). I do not claim it.
5. Low: not applicable, R7 is violated (undocumented departure).
candidates.threat_to_goal: No effect on hashes or proofs (consistent across paths). It violates R7: the architecture executed is a superset of the one the manual documents, and for four encodings a superset of what the ratified Zcb allows without Zbb/Zba, so a guest written to the manual observes different trap behaviour.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERSPEC/isa.lua: 0x9c71 (c.zext.w x8), 0x9c65 (c.sext.b), 0x9c69 (c.zext.h), 0x9c6d (c.sext.h), 0x9c75 (c.not), 0x9c45 (c.mul), 0x9c61 (c.zext.b) each advance pc to 0x80000002 with mcause=0 and the Zcb result in x8; the 32-bit add.uw (0x0804043b, Zba) and sext.b (0x60441413, Zbb) raise mcause=2. grep -i zcb doc/README.md: no match.
candidates.test_idea: Lua: for each Zcb encoding write it at 0x80000000, run one mcycle and assert mcause == 2 (illegal instruction) and mtval == the 16-bit encoding, as the documented RV64IMAFDC requires; or, if Zcb is to stay, assert the manual lists it and that c.sext.b/c.zext.h/c.sext.h/c.zext.w trap while Zbb/Zba are absent. Fails today.

candidates.title: Writing the mcycle CSR in M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception although the privileged specification makes mcycle read-write, and the manual documents no deviation
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp write_csr_mcycle (lines 2405-2414, returns execute_status::failure) dispatched from write_csr (2561-2562); doc/README.md 'The main processor' (7358-7362) describes mcycle without mentioning it.
candidates.description: CSR 0xB00 (mcycle) is MRW in the privileged specification: an M-mode CSRRW/CSRRS/CSRRC that writes it must succeed. The emulator makes every write trap with cause 2 ('We instead raise an exception', source comment). The reason is sound (mcycle is the protocol clock, R8: the guest 'can never change the cycle counter'), but R7 allows a departure only 'where the manual documents a deviation', and the manual is silent. minstret (0xB02) is writable as specified.
candidates.trigger: M-mode guest code (firmware, bare-metal runtime) executing e.g. 'csrw mcycle, x0' — a legal way to reset the cycle counter. It takes an unexpected M-mode trap; with no handler installed (mtvec = 0 at reset) control goes to address 0 and the machine spins on instruction access faults instead of processing the input.
candidates.reachability: Any state in M-mode; reachable by any firmware/bare-metal guest.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no (emulator behaviour triggered by a guest instruction).
2. Role: interpreter = Honest operator.

3. High/Medium cases: matches "An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)." (no isolation or integrity reliance on writing mcycle).

4. Critical: only under a strict reading of R7: "The emulator implements the RISC-V specification and the devices as the manual documents them, departing only where the manual documents a deviation." with the listed area 'Traps and interrupts' (a trap the specification does not allow). Not claimed.
5. Low: not applicable, R7 is violated.
candidates.threat_to_goal: No effect on hashes or proofs. Violates R7 (undocumented departure from the ratified privileged specification in a CSR every M-mode guest may legally write).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERSPEC/isa.lua: 'csrw mcycle,x0' (0xb0001073) at reset in M-mode -> pc=0x0 (mtvec), mcause=2, mtval=0xb0001073; 'csrw minstret,x0' (0xb0201073) -> pc=0x80000004, mcause=0. grep of the manual for a documented deviation (illegal instruction / read-only mcycle) finds nothing.
candidates.test_idea: Lua: write 0xb0001073 at 0x80000000, run one mcycle; assert either mcause == 0 and pc == 0x80000004 (write accepted or ignored, as the specification's MRW requires) or that the manual documents that writes to mcycle trap. Fails today on both counts.

candidates.title: Manual's /dev/cmio description says the next request's type is returned in the yield's data field, while the HTIF section and the emulator return it in the reason field (data carries the length)
candidates.component: Manual (doc/README.md, 'The /dev/cmio device') versus input delivery (send_cmio_response) and the HTIF section of the same manual
candidates.role: Honest operator (input delivery writes htif fromhost); the manual is the specification of the yield interface
candidates.location: doc/README.md lines 7234-7239 ('HTIF_YIELD_MANUAL_REASON_RX_ACCEPTED (... the host sets the `data` field on resume to HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE or HTIF_YIELD_REASON_INSPECT_STATE to indicate the type of the freshly loaded input in the receive buffer)') versus lines 7665-7668 ('The REASON field in fromhost carries the request type, and the DATA field carries the request length in bytes'); src/send-cmio-response.cpp lines 78-82 (fromhost = (reason & 0xffff) << 32 | dataLength); machine-guest-tools libcmt/io.h ('Reply reason when requesting ...').
candidates.description: The yield interface is one of the R7 areas ('contents, lengths, and reason encoding'). The manual gives two incompatible encodings of the response to an accept/reject yield. The HTIF section and the code put the request type (advance 0 / inspect 1) in REASON (bits 47-32) and the request length in DATA (bits 31-0). The /dev/cmio section, which documents struct cmio_yield {dev, cmd, reason, data} for tooling that talks to the device directly, says the host sets the data field to the request type. A guest written to that paragraph reads the input length as the request type: a 1-byte advance-state input would be taken for an inspect-state request, any other non-empty input for an unknown type (the manual's own guest loop then rejects it), and only empty inputs for advance.
candidates.trigger: A guest or binding that uses the raw /dev/cmio ioctl (or HTIF directly) and follows the /dev/cmio paragraph; then any input sender controls the 'type' the guest sees through the input length.
candidates.reachability: Every delivery: the emulator always writes type to REASON and length to DATA.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no. Not an application-design exclusion: the guest follows the manual as written.
2. Role: input delivery = Honest operator; the defect is in the manual, which section 8 rates through the contradiction clause.

3. High/Medium cases: "A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right." Here the manual contradicts itself; the code agrees with the HTIF section. If the HTIF section is taken as the manual's word, this is a documentation error with no rule violated by the emulator (Low/Medium).
4. Critical: if the /dev/cmio sentence were right, delivery would violate R7 in a listed area: "The rx buffer, the tx buffer, and the yield interface (contents, lengths, and reason encoding)."
5. Low: the alternative reading. Deciding fact: which of the two manual passages is normative for guests that bypass libcmt.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Low if the HTIF section is taken as the only normative text; Critical under the literal 'as if the manual were right' reading of the /dev/cmio sentence)
candidates.threat_to_goal: A guest written exactly to the /dev/cmio paragraph misclassifies every non-empty input (the sender chooses the misreading by choosing the length), so it deviates from the rollup interface although it follows the manual; the settled state then differs from what its author specified. No hash or proof is affected.
candidates.evidence: Read doc/README.md 7234-7239 and 7665-7668, src/send-cmio-response.cpp (yieldData), and the libcmt io.h shipped in machine-guest-tools v0.18.1-test1 (extracted to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERSPEC/gt/usr/include/libcmt/io.h): cmt_io_yield_t {dev, cmd, reason, data} with 'Reply reason when requesting HTIF_YIELD_MANUAL_REASON_RX_ACCEPTED or HTIF_YIELD_MANUAL_REASON_RX_REJECTED: HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE = 0, HTIF_YIELD_REASON_INSPECT_STATE = 1'. Not run.
candidates.test_idea: Lua: on a valid template deliver an advance-state input of length 1 with send_cmio_response, then read htif_fromhost and assert that the field the /dev/cmio section names (data, bits 31-0) equals HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE; it equals the length instead. Equivalent documentation test: assert the two manual passages name the same field.

candidates.title: Guest-visible architecture exceeds the manual: Sv48 translation is accepted (manual and device tree say Sv39 only) and the CLINT msip register is active (manual lists only mtime and mtimecmp as active)
candidates.component: Interpreter (satp/address translation) and CLINT device versus the manual
candidates.location: Sv48: src/translate-virtual-address.hpp lines 136-148, src/interpret.cpp write_csr_satp (2247-2262), src/riscv-warl.hpp WARL_satp, src/dtb.cpp line 105 (mmu-type = riscv,sv39); doc/README.md 7312-7315 ('Cartesi Machines support the Sv39 mode of address translation ... three-level page table'). msip: src/clint-address-range.cpp clint_csr::msip0 = 0, do_write_device (sets/clears mip.MSIP, 4-byte access); doc/README.md 7525-7527 ('The active addresses are 0x0200bff8 (mtime) and 0x02004000 (mtimecmp)').
candidates.description: (a) satp.MODE = 9 (Sv48) is accepted and a four-level walk is performed; the manual describes only Sv39 with a three-level table and the device tree advertises riscv,sv39. Virtual addresses that are non-canonical under Sv39 (and must page-fault there) translate under Sv48. (b) A 4-byte store of 1 to 0x02000000 sets mip.MSIP and, when enabled, raises a machine software interrupt; the manual's CLINT section says the only active addresses are mtime and mtimecmp, so a guest following it expects an access fault there (as at every other CLINT offset). Both are legal RISC-V/CLINT behaviour, but they are guest-visible behaviour in two R7 areas (address translation; traps and interrupts) that the manual does not document. Two independent items, listed together because each is minor; triage may split them.
candidates.trigger: (a) S- or M-mode guest code writing satp with MODE=9. (b) Any guest code that can reach the CLINT page writing offset 0.
candidates.reachability: Any state; registers and memory are guest-writable.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no.
2. Role: interpreter and devices = Honest operator.

3. High/Medium cases: matches "An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)." satp is under the control of the same privilege level that would be 'surprised', and msip only reaches a hart that mapped the CLINT, so no correct guest relies on the absence of either.

4. Critical: not claimed; a strict reading of R7: "The emulator implements the RISC-V specification and the devices as the manual documents them, departing only where the manual documents a deviation." (devices 'as the manual documents them') would count both as undocumented departures in listed areas.
5. Low: if the manual's sentences are read as non-exhaustive descriptions rather than as a specification of what is absent.
candidates.threat_to_goal: No effect on hashes or proofs. R7: the manual is the specification of the devices and of the supported translation modes; behaviour outside it is undocumented. The Sv48 item also matters for cost reviews: a four-level walk adds page-table accesses to a uarch step beyond what a reader of the manual would size for (not measured).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERSPEC/isa.lua and msip.lua: 'csrw satp' with MODE=9 reads back 0x9000000000000000 (MODE=10 is ignored, MODE=8 accepted); with a four-level table a load at 0x0000400000000000 under MPRV/MPP=S returns the mapped doubleword with mcause=0; 'sw 1 -> 0x02000000' leaves pc=0x80000004, mcause=0, mip=0x8 (MSIP).
candidates.test_idea: Lua: (a) write satp with MODE=9 from M-mode and assert it reads back with the previous mode (the write has no effect, as for an unsupported mode), matching the manual and the device tree; (b) store 1 to 0x02000000 and assert a store access fault (mcause 7) and mip unchanged, or assert that the manual documents msip. Both fail today.

not_covered: machine-guest-tools sources (libcmt, rollup, rollup-http-server, cartesi-init, yield): only the shipped libcmt/io.h header was read; no guest-software audit.
The Linux /dev/cmio driver and OpenSBI (out of scope) were not read, so the reason/data mapping of the ioctl was inferred from libcmt/io.h and the emulator's fromhost encoding.

Dynamic multi-instruction tests of privilege, TLB flushing (MPRV/MPP, SUM, MXR, satp, SFENCE.VMA), interrupt delivery and delegation, and LR/SC were not run; these were checked by reading src/interpret.cpp and translate-virtual-address.hpp only (no deviation found). All probes were single instructions through machine:run on the native interpreter.
uarch-versus-native agreement (R2) of the behaviours examined; the on-chain step; logs and proofs.

Floating point: src/soft-float.hpp was compared with host x86-64 SSE/FMA on 4,000,000 special-value-heavy samples per operation for add, sub, mul, div, sqrt, fma, f32<->f64, int<->float, comparisons, min/max and fclass in RNE/RTZ/RDN/RUP (only difference: fma(0, inf, qNaN) sets NV, which RISC-V requires and x86 does not). The RMM rounding mode was tested only for float-to-integer conversions; FP instruction decoding (rm field, NaN boxing) was read, not tested.
Integer, M-extension and base C-extension semantics and immediates were spot-read, not tested (assumed covered by riscv-tests).

PLIC and VirtIO behaviour (only reachable with pending sources, i.e. unreproducible machines), including the shared software/PLIC SEIP bit that a source comment already describes as a deviation; HTIF console input; the soft-yield hint (SRAIW x0, x31) under the interactive runtime option.

LR/SC: the reservation is tracked by virtual address and survives same-privilege traps and satp changes; judged within what the specification leaves to software, not tested against aliasing or remapping.

Device-tree contents beyond the isa and mmu-type strings. Flash drive and NVRAM placement rules: observed, but not reported as a candidate (configuration, not guest behaviour; five-candidate limit), that the emulator accepts a flash drive at 0x90001000 of length 0x1000 and one at 0x70000000 below RAM, although the manual says 'Flash drives must start after 0x80000000+ram.length-1, end before 0x80000000+64TiB, and be aligned to 2MiB'; not followed up.
The host and blockchain perspectives of the manual (hash views, output proofs, PRT) and every referee, operator and persistence component: outside this angle.
Sv57 (compiled out), PMP, hypervisor, vector and debug CSRs: only confirmed absent by reading the CSR switch.
